analytic.title: A Heuristic-based Dynamic Scheduling and Routing Method for Industrial TSN Networks

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: In the industrial environment, machines often need to reflect the anomaly detection results to the total control center in time, and the general industrial network can not achieve high real-time. In order to solve such challenges, a set of protocol standards developed by IEEE802.1 working group, namely Time-sensitive Networking (TSN), has been introduced into industrial networks. TSN can provide high realtime and reliability for data transmission, where the reliability is achieved by Frame duplication and Frame Elimination (FRER). In the realization process of FRER, it is necessary to determine the source node, destination node, and multiple disjoint paths to transmit redundant data. However, the transmission of these redundant traffic may result in the delay of other flows, and then affects the user experience. Therefore, it is very important to choose excellent redundant traffic paths to ensure reliability and reduce the impact on other flows. In the existing research, there are many dynamic scheduling and routing heuristics to determine the path, but they do not consider the influence of the location of the source node on the whole route scheduling. This paper proposes an improved dynamic scheduling and routing heuristic method, which takes the source node into account in the routing selection. In the flow test experiments of different magnitudes, it is found that the total delay of all flows is reduced by 1.4%-4.5% under the same magnitude of schedulability compared with Ant Colony Optimization.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: With the deepening of industrial automation, many automatic or semi-automatic machines have been used in industrial quality testing. These machines for the transmission of information to microsecond level, and then also for the transmission of data information of industrial Ethernet put forward high time synchronization, high reliability, high quality of service (Qos) and other requirements. Therefore, it is necessary to enhance the optimization of Ethernet. In the industry, many Ethernet technologies have been proposed, and Time-sensitive Networking meets this requirement [1]. For example, TSN-based Industrial Internet of things for underground mining [2].

Time-sensitive network is made up of IEEE802.1 AS, IEEE802.1 Qbv, IEEE802.1 CB, IEEE802.1 Qci, IEEE802.1 Qch and a series of agreements of the Ethernet protocol defined standards [3]. The characteristics of TSN network are end-to-end deterministic delay, high quality of service and high reliability. IEEE802.1AS standard is a time synchronization protocol, which provides support for endto-end deterministic delay in the network. TSN supports three different types of traffic which are Time-triggered (TT) streams, Audio-video Bridging (AVB) streams, and Best-effort (BE) streams. In industrial application scenarios, safety-critical data will be generated and transmitted by safety-related applications or machines, such as power, braking, steering information flow, and unmanned working environment sensing data flow. These safety flows are often regarded as redundant traffic and need to be transmitted redundancies. These flows can also BE classified as TT, AVB, or BE flows, depending on their latency. Both AVB flows and BE flows are non-preemptible flows. The creditbased shaping (Cbs) algorithm proposed in IEEE802.1 AVB is used to determine which flow to transmit.

In the new industrial system, there are often a large number of data streams that need to be transmitted and exchange at the terminal of the machine. In IEEE802.1 Qbv [4], the time-aware shaper (TAS) is introduced. The shaper sets a gate control list (GCL) to control the flow exit from a specific port [5]. The port is closed when the gate is 0. TAS also proposes a guard-band mechanism to ensure the real-time transmission of time-sensitive flows in case of interference by other flows, but the guard band should not be too large to prevent affecting other flow transmission [6]. There are many schedules in a network. For example, on embedded systems with multiple ECUs, there are schedules within ECUs and schedules between ECUs [7]. In industrial Ethernet, there is a Central Network Controller (CNC) that handles all the gating list setup and routing scheduling.

In IEEE802.1 Qbu, frame preemption mechanism is proposed, which enables the time-sensitive flow to interrupt the non-TT flow when it arrives at the waiting queue and then transmit, which further ensures the real-time transmission of TT flow. The transmission of safety-critical data frames in industrial networks needs to take into account various unexpected situations such as packet loss and packet error. Therefore, the frame duplication and frame elimination protocol proposed in IEEE 802.1CB protocol is used in TSN to increase the fault tolerance ability, but the protocol does not propose how to obtain redundant paths for transmission duplicates [8]. Therefore, many different redundant path calculation algorithms have been published. The routing of redundant traffic will be determined by the path selection algorithm, and different paths will affect the scheduling and transmission delay of other flows. For example, high-priority traffic can have a significant impact on the delay of besteffort flows [9]. The contribution of this paper is to take the source node selection into account in the routing of redundant traffic scheduling, and then improve the routing algorithm to reduce the overall flow delay and maximize the flow schedulability.

The rest of this paper is organized as follows. In section II, we describe the work of other researchers on routing algorithms. Section III presents the proposed system model. Section IV presents the formulation description and optimized heuristic algorithm of the dynamic scheduling and routing selection problem for the flow. Section V will carry out experiments to verify the proposed algorithm and analyze the experimental results, and finally the paper will be concluded in Section VI.

div.head: II. RELATED WORK
div.p: In recent years, more and more attention has been paid to TSN, and the scheduling and routing of traffic in TSN have also come into people's vision. In [10], the authors proposed a routing heuristic and a scheduling heuristic to generate redundant transmission paths and schedules for time-sensitive traffic, respectively. And a joint optimization algorithm is proposed to optimize routing and scheduling to accommodate the random and dynamic events of real networks. In [11], the authors proposed a load-balanced routing model in time-sensitive networks to reduce circuit latency. Aiming at the joint optimization problem in practical communication scenarios, LiuYang et al. [12] proposed a deep reinforcement learning based on graph convolutional network to obtain transmission paths and schedules. The authors focused on static traffic and devices in [13] and proposed a novel static scheduling and routing algorithm that facilitates dynamic traffic demands. In this approach, the authors developed joint scheduling and routing for static applications based on mixed integer programming (MIP) with the aim of load balancing so that more dynamic traffic can be scheduled when vehicles move away.

In [14], The authors analyzed four carefully designed heuristics for dynamic scheduling and dynamic routing in TSN-based IVNs. One of the algorithms, the bottleneck heuristic outperforms the others in terms of schedulability and response time. In [15], The authors proposed an Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) based approach to explore the online routing problem considering TSN and AVB traffic in TSN networks. The vehicular network studied by the authors in [16], proposed four different dynamic scheduling and routing heuristics to support FRER functionality in TSN-based IVNs. These heuristics used combined score values, each dedicated to a single path, as a measure for dynamically scheduling and routing incoming flows in multiple redundant paths. One of the algorithms, Fault-tolerant Bottleneck Heuristic (FTBH) outperforms the others in terms of schedulability and response time. In these studies, the selection of starting distribution nodes for redundant routing transmission paths has not been studied. Therefore, compared with other related algorithms, we focus on the scheduling of redundant traffic. A new decision method is also proposed in the scheduling of redundant traffic. We have designed an optimized heuristic algorithm to support the source node selection of the FRER function and obtain the transmission path and dynamic scheduling of the final redundant traffic.

div.head: A. Routing Algorithm
div.p: In this section, we present our dynamic scheduling and heuristic algorithms designed to solve the scheduling problem of TT flows, AVB flows, BE flows as well as redundant traffic. In TSN network, when a new flow is transmitted from the source endpoint to the network, the master controller will receive all the label information related to the flow, but does not read the flow data. The master controller first obtains K paths according to the start and end points of the flow through the Yens algorithm, and then the master controller presets that the flow will use the K path to transmit, because when the flow chooses a certain path to transmit, it will affect the transmission of other flows on the path, and then affect the completion time of these flows. Therefore, depending on the size of the impact, this test will receive a score, and the score is calculated using Equation ( 6). After completing K tests, the master controller will select the one with the highest score as the final scheduling route.

div.head: Algorithm 1 AdapterNode Algorithm
div.formula: Input: S, Bridges, G < E, V > Output: Bridges for i = 1 to n do K ← Y ensAlgo(G, S i ) if S i .redundent = 1 then K ← SelectK(G, K) Bridges1 ← AssumeAdd(K , Bridges, S i ) g ← Score(K , Bridges1, S i ) else Bridges2 ← AssumeAdd(K, Bridges, S i ) g ← Score(K, Bridges2, S i ) end if Bridges ← AddS(Bridges, S i , K g ) end for
div.p: When the traffic is redundant, K paths are obtained by the Yens algorithm, and then the branch path of each path is found by the SelectK() function, and the K paths and their branch paths are scored once. Finally, the distribution starting node and the final redundant path of the redundant traffic are determined according to the score list, and the redundancy magnitude of the redundant traffic is 1. The pseudo-code of the AdapterNode algorithm is presented in Algorithm 1. For example, in Fig. 3, when there is a redundant traffic S, starting point is a and ending point is b, two paths (a,b,f,d) and (a,e,d,f) can be obtained by Yens algorithm, and then the branch path (b,c,d) of (a,b,f,d) can be found by SelectK() function. Therefore, three paths will be taken as input into the test score function. Finally, the distribution starting point is b, and the routes of redundant traffic are (a,b,f,d) and (b,c,d). div.head: A. Preparation for the experiment
div.p: In this section, we present the experiments and evaluation of the adaptive node scheduling algorithm, the scheduling algorithm is implemented in python, and the experiments are run on a 64-bit Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-8250U CPU @ 1.60GHz, 1.80 GHz environment with 8GB memory. We use the total delay and schedulability under different load conditions as performance evaluation criteria, traffic is divided into TT flow, AVB flow, BE flow, redundant traffic is security sensitive flow, may be any of the three kinds of traffic, redundant traffic will have two redundant routes.

According to previous work, the data size of each TSN stream is between 1,500 and 4.500 bytes. The data size of each AVB stream is set to 400 bytes. The period of each flow is set to 100, 200, or 250 microseconds. The deadline of each flow is equal to its period. The link capacity is set to 1Gbps and the timeout for each run is set to 10-100ms. If not mentioned, the default timeout is 10 milliseconds [15]. The results on each report are the average of 100 independent runs on the experimental environment. The computation time of each final run is set to be the hyperperiod computed by the least common multiple of all flow cycles.

The topology of the experiment is six nodes, each node is dual-channel with each other, and there is a transmission delay between the nodes Fig. 4. The network load level is divided into low and medium and high. The low load is set to 2 TT flows, 13 AVB flows, and 5 BE flows. The medium load is 6 TT flows, 25 AVB flows, and 13 BE flows. The high load is 6 TT flows, 39AVB flows, and 19 BE flows.

div.head: B. Comparison algorithm
div.p: Ant Colony Optimization(ACO) routing scheduling algorithm: it uses the Yens algorithm to narrow the search domain, uses the optimized ant colony algorithm to select the path, and uses the Cbs and TAS traffic shaper in the switch [15]. Since the algorithm does not consider the redundant

div.head: C. Experiment 1
div.p: The comparison experiment between ACO algorithm and adaptive node redundancy algorithm shows that the first algorithm fixed the end node of redundant traffic routing selection as the starting point and the end point of traffic distribution, and the second algorithm judged the redundant nodes according to the network load. The two algorithms are tested with different workloads, and the results are compared in the schedulability, total delay, these two evaluation indicators. The experimental results are shown in Fig. 5 and Fig. 6.

Through the experimental results, Ant Colony Optimization can BE seen that all flows are schedulable flows at low load, and only 98 percent are schedulable flows at medium load, in which all flows of TT flow are schedulable, AVB flow has 1 unschedulable flow, BE flow has no unschedulable flow, the total algorithm computation time is 45.2ms, and the total target score is 212. It also achieves 100% schedulability at high workloads, the total algorithm computation time is 31.44ms, and the total target fraction is 267. Overall, it can be seen from the table that as the load increases, the flow unschedulable situation also occurs in Algorithm 1. In algorithm 2, all flows are schedulable at low load, and the total computation time is 3.5ms. In algorithm 2, 98% of flows are schedulable at medium load, in which all flows of TT flow are schedulable, one flow of AVB flow is not schedulable, and all flows of BE flow are schedulable. The total computation time is 44.8ms, and the total objective score is 220. In the second algorithm, 98.5% of the flows are schedulable when the load is high, among which all the TT flows are schedulable, one AVB flow is not schedulable, and all BE flows are schedulable. The total computation time is 27.9ms, and the delay score is 271. Compared with Algorithm 1, under the same order of schedulability, the total delay is decreased by 1.4%-4.5%, and the computing time is also reduced by about 7.5%.

div.head: VI. CONCLUSION
div.p: In this paper, we have proposed a dynamic scheduling and routing algorithm for adaptive nodes that fully considers the time-aware shaping capabilities of the FRER and IEEETSN standards. The total delay and schedulability under different loads are used as new performance metrics to verify the effectiveness of the algorithm. The redundancy level of the redundant traffic in the scheduled traffic is one. Compared with the ACO algorithm, the total delay of the adaptive node algorithm is decreased by 1.4%-4.5%, and the computing time is reduced by about 7.5% under the same order of schedulability.
